sources.entry: Focus Firewall - A minimalist focus app to block social media and other distractions during work. [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6476942786?pt=124015613&ct=awesome-mac&mt=8&platform=mac)

summary.name: Focus Firewall
summary.one_liner: A macOS app that blocks distracting websites and apps such as X, Instagram, YouTube, and Reddit on a schedule, at the system level.
use_cases: Block social media during work hours
Stop YouTube and Reddit from loading on a schedule
Limit procrastination while working on a Mac
Block distracting sites across all browsers
Track time spent on websites with and without blocking
Block specific messaging apps during focus time
summary.what_it_does: Focus Firewall blocks websites and apps on a Mac according to schedules the user sets. It works at the system level, so it does not need a browser extension and applies across many browsers, including Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Arc, Brave, and Edge. It ships with a list of 155+ websites and 9 messaging apps, and users can add their own. Users can pause blocking for ten minutes, turn off a category, or unblock a single site. A browsing report shows time per site, hour by hour, with blocking on or off. The page states that no account is needed and that data stays on the Mac.
notable: System-level blocking that works in any browser without extensions
Pause that automatically re-enables blocking after ten minutes
Hour-by-hour browsing report that compares time with blocking on and off
No account and no data collected; blocking happens locally
caveats: Paid: $2.99/month, $19.99/year, or $29.99 one-time Lifetime; a 7-day free trial is offered
macOS only; iPhone and iPad version is only being considered
Browsers not on the supported list need to be requested by email
